findings.body: math.floor() or math.ceil() receives a datetime value, raising TypeError and returning an unhandled 500 response instead of audit-log results.
findings.failure_mode: The newly selectable optimized audit-log path fails while constructing the cursor for any non-empty result set.
findings.impact: math.floor() or math.ceil() receives a datetime value, raising TypeError and returning an unhandled 500 response instead of audit-log results.
findings.root_cause: The new paginator copied numeric-key rounding logic into a path that is used with DateTimePaginator-compatible datetime model fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse DateTimePaginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor for this endpoint, or make OptimizedCursorPaginator convert datetime keys to the same millisecond integer representation before rounding.
findings.title: Optimized paginator crashes on datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.trigger: An authorized administrator requests the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination=true while at least one audit-log row exists; the paginator is ordered by the datetime field.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key at line 838-840 which calls math.floor/ceil on value=getattr(item, self.key). The endpoint uses order_by='-datetime' with AuditLogEntry which has a datetime field. DateTimePaginator converts datetime to float first (line 235), but OptimizedCursorPaginator does not - it passes datetime directly to math.floor/ceil which raises TypeError.

findings.impact: Django QuerySet negative slicing raises ValueError because negative indexing is unsupported; paginate does not translate this exception, so the request returns an unhandled 500 response.

findings.suggested_fix: Reject negative offsets with BadPaginationError, or normalize them before slicing; implement reverse pagination through ordering and cursor predicates rather than negative QuerySet indices.
findings.title: Negative optimized cursors produce an unhandled queryset slicing error
findings.trigger: A client sends an optimized audit-log request with a cursor containing a negative forward offset, such as 0:-1:0.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines 877-882 show that when enable_advanced_features=True and cursor.offset<0, the code uses start_offset=cursor.offset directly in queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets raise ValueError on negative slice indices. The endpoint passes enable_advanced_features=True (line 82), so a crafted cursor with negative offset triggers this.

findings.body: Redis raises WRONGTYPE when the new worker executes ZADD against the old set, causing span processing to fail and leaving buffered spans unprocessed.
findings.failure_mode: Existing queued data becomes unreadable or unwritable as soon as a new worker encounters it.

findings.root_cause: The patch changes the Redis data type for persistent span-buffer keys without migrating or isolating keys created by the previous implementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a versioned key namespace or add a migration/read-through conversion from sets to sorted sets before issuing ZADD/ZSCAN, while keeping mixed-version workers safe during rollout.

raw_findings.body: The Lua script retains up to 1000 spans and the loader no longer enforces the configured limit, so segments exceed the caller's size bound and can consume more memory and processing capacity than intended.
raw_findings.evidence:
if span_count > 1000 then
    redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)
end
raw_findings.failure_mode: Configuration intended to bound segment span count silently has no effect.
raw_findings.impact: The Lua script retains up to 1000 spans and the loader no longer enforces the configured limit, so segments exceed the caller's size bound and can consume more memory and processing capacity than intended.
raw_findings.root_cause: Eviction was hard-coded to 1000 while the existing configurable max_segment_spans enforcement was removed.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the configured max_segment_spans into the script and evict to that value, or restore an equivalent count check in _load_segment_data; do not leave the constructor option unused.
raw_findings.title: The configured max_segment_spans limit is ignored
raw_findings.trigger: A caller constructs SpansBuffer with max_segment_spans below 1000, such as max_segment_spans=10, and a segment accumulates more than that configured number of spans.

raw_findings.body: Redis's default ZUNIONSTORE aggregation sums the duplicate member's end-timestamp scores, making it appear newer; when the cap is exceeded, ZPOPMIN can evict a different, genuinely oldest span instead.
raw_findings.evidence:
span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)
    redis.call("unlink", span_key)
end

local parent_key = string.format("span-buf:s:{%s}:%s", project_and_trace, parent_span_id)
if set_span_id ~= parent_span_id and redis.call("zcard", parent_key) > 0 then
    span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)
raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate members alter ordering metadata and cause eviction to discard the wrong buffered spans.
raw_findings.impact: Redis's default ZUNIONSTORE aggregation sums the duplicate member's end-timestamp scores, making it appear newer; when the cap is exceeded, ZPOPMIN can evict a different, genuinely oldest span instead.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new sorted-set merge uses ZUNIONSTORE's default SUM aggregation even though scores represent timestamps rather than additive quantities.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an explicit non-summing aggregation such as AGGREGATE MIN for these unions, or otherwise preserve the member's original eviction score when merging sets.
raw_findings.title: Sorted-set union sums duplicate span scores and corrupts eviction order
raw_findings.trigger: A delayed or duplicate span causes the same payload member to exist in both the destination set and a set being merged during redirect resolution.

raw_findings.body: The loop exits before reaching the terminal segment, so the new span is assigned to an intermediate set and the trace can be split across segments instead of being joined correctly.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Deep but valid parent chains silently resolve to the wrong segment rather than producing a controlled failure.
raw_findings.impact: The loop exits before reaching the terminal segment, so the new span is assigned to an intermediate set and the trace can be split across segments instead of being joined correctly.
raw_findings.root_cause: The redirect-depth limit was reduced from 10000 to 1000 without adding overflow handling or proving that supported traces cannot exceed the new bound.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Retain the previous traversal bound or make the bound consistent with the maximum supported tree depth; detect overflow explicitly instead of treating the unresolved intermediate ID as final.
raw_findings.title: Redirect traversal now truncates at roughly 1000 levels
raw_findings.trigger: A trace contains a redirect chain requiring more than 1001 parent-resolution hops, such as a deeply nested segment tree or a long sequence of late parent merges.
